construction_notes.text: From the state Housing Element Annual Progress Report, through 2025.

City of San Jose permit PD21-020 (Planned Development Permit/Amendment, folder year 2021), status Approved, issue date 2025-06-17: "Planned Development Permit to allow the removal of four trees (three ordinance-size) and the construction of three buildings on two separate parcels, for a total of 16 multi-family residential condominium units, including seven live-work units on a cumula" (city text cut off at 255 characters)

City of San Jose permit T23-010 (Tentative Map, folder year 2023), status Approved: "Vesting Tentative Map to allow for up to 16 residential condominium units, including up to 10 units on the approximately 0.54-gross-acre lot (APN 659-57-015), and up to six units on the approximately 0.27-gross-acre lot (APN 659-84-093) in association wit" (city text cut off at 255 characters)

City of San Jose permit PDA21-020-01 (Planned Development Permit/Amendment, folder year 2026), status Under Review: "Planned Development Permit Amendment to change location of one live work unit, reduce the total unit count from 16 to 14, and change the units from condominiums to townhomes."
Site is two vacant parcels at Classico Avenue and Evergreen Village Square, San Jose 95135 (APNs 659-57-015 and 659-84-093). City permit records show no street address ("0 Land Only").

City permit records list HawkStone Development (Reyad Katwan) as applicant and owner on the 2021-2023 files; QM Investments LLC (Thanh Nguyen) on the 2026 amendment, environmental review ER26-109 and tentative map files; and HILL/HO/PANG/NGUENPHUC/PANG (Anthony Ho) on a 2025 preliminary review for 13 units.
CEQAnet lists Denise Duffy & Associates as the environmental consultant and Cort Hitchens as the city planner.
